newsitem.title: USA: El Paso, National Fuel seek to build USG gas line.
newsitem.headline: El Paso, National Fuel seek to build USG gas line.

text.p: El Paso Energy Resources and National Fuel Gas Supply Corp have agreed to jointly seek approval during the second quarter of 1997 to build about 150 miles of gas pipeline in the U.S. Gulf, El Paso said Wednesday.
If approved by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), the new Green Canyon Gathering System will likely begin delivering gas from the producing region in 1998, El Paso said in a statement.

The pipeline will provide offshore producers with two-phase transportation of approximately 16,000 barrels per day of natural gas liquids and more than 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas.

A cryogenic processing plant will also be constructed in Golden Meadown, La., as part of the project. The plant, which will not be subject to FERC jurisdiction, will have the capability of processing 300 mmcfd of natural gas.
An open season for transportation capacity on the Green Canyon system will be conducted after the application has been filed with FERC.
El Paso Energy Resources is a subsidiary of El Paso Energy Corp while National Fuel is a unit of National Fuel Gas Co.
